newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Iraq pushes to speed up food-for-oil sales.
newsitem.headline: Iraq pushes to speed up food-for-oil sales.

text.p: An Iraqi minister said on Wednesday that Baghdad was mounting a diplomatic offensive to push for sales under the United Nations food-for-oil plan to be speeded up.

Culture and Information Minister Hamed Youssef Hummadi, addressing a news conference in the Moroccan capital, accused the United States of blocking contracts and said Iraq wanted Arab countries to be more active in helping it.
"I do not understand that countries like Russia or France are more active than Arab countries," he said.

Hummadi said Washington constantly opposed approval of Iraqi trade deals with other countries as well as opposing the lifting of the trade embargo imposed on Iraq over its 1990 invasion and seven-month-long occupation of Kuwait.
"We have submitted to the United Nations 240 contracts so far. Only 15 have been approved because the United States rejects them," the minister said.
Last December the United Nations approved a food-for-oil plan, allowing Iraq to sell up to $2 billion worth of oil in six months in order to buy food and humanitarian aid for its people.
Hummadi said the number of children dying had increased sevenfold since 1990, with a fourfold increase among adults.
